title: A Methodology to Extract Knowledge from Datasets Using ML
content: This study aims to verify whether there is any relationship between the different classification outputs produced by distinct ML algorithms and the relevance of the data they classify, for addressing the problem of the knowledge extraction (KE) from datasets. If such relationship existed, the main objective of this research is to use it in order to improve performance in the important task of KE from datasets. A new dataset generation and a new ML classification measurement methodology were developed to check whether the feature subsets (FSs) best classified by a specific ML algorithm correspond to the most KE-relevant combinations of features. Medical expertise was extracted to check knowledge relevance using two LLMs, namely chat GPT and Google Gemini. Some specific ML algorithms fit much better than others for a working dataset extracted from a given probability distribution. They best classify FSs that contain combinations of features particularly knowledge relevant. This implies that using a specific ML algorithm we can indeed extract useful scientific knowledge. The best-fitting ML algorithm is not known a priori. However, we can bootstrap its identity using a small amount of medical expertise, and we have a powerful tool for extracting (medical) knowledge from datasets using ML.
